Hi! I'm Magnus.

Practitechnical Academic and Swiss Multitool

I work as an Associate Professor at Roskilde University where I get to design and develop: tech tools that produce value for practitioners, server infrastructure for local InfoSec projects, local LLM testing and Open Source Enterprise tools. The best part is that I get to publish the results !
Often I get the notion that I am too practical for academics and too academic for practice but it has gotten me a lot of useful research projects with practitioners and external companies and a very strong hands-on approach.

About me

I am an all-out nice guy with a passion for working with people and technology, especially Linux-based infrastructure, to enable the coolest and most delicious technical solutions!
I know how to build most things from scratch and I love the challenge of figuring out how it fits into your organisation!

I know a lot but I also know that I do not know everything, and I know that I can start learning mostly everything as long as it has a purpose and someone finds it useful!
Check out how I do what I do!

My job experience

2018- now
Associate Professor
Roskilde University. Roskilde, Denmark

Job #5

5th job: Associate Professor at the Department of People and Technology As Chief Information Officer at Internet Affairs Inc., I lead the strategic transformation of our digital infrastructure and cybersecurity initiatives. My team of 150+ IT professionals works tirelessly to protect and optimize our global network spanning 23 countries. During my tenure, I’ve spearheaded the implementation of a revolutionary blockchain-based verification system that reduced fraudulent transactions by 87% while improving processing speeds by 300%. This initiative saved the company $12M annually and earned us the prestigious “Digital Innovation Award 2024”. I’m particularly proud of our “Green Computing” program which has successfully migrated 75% of our data centers to renewable energy sources. This environmental initiative not only reduced our carbon footprint by 45% but also resulted in a 30% reduction in operational costs. In my role, I also serve as a member of the executive board, helping shape the company’s long-term technology vision and ensuring our IT strategy aligns perfectly with our business objectives. Currently leading an ambitious AI integration project that promises to revolutionize our customer service capabilities.

1st job: Technical supporter for Apple and Macintosh servers and desktops Beginning as a student helper I managed the backup servers (Retrospect) for the Macintosh computers at our department, ranging about 10 users. I had the opportunity to familiarize myself with the basics of Unix commands and server level hardware and software as well as solving technical troubleshooting tasks such as repairing work stations and arranging and scheduling backups on a weekly basis. From this job began my own interest in Unix-like systems and ensured that I could navigate later on in my Master of Computer Science where I could setup SVN servers, use LaTeX and got into Emacs. I also learned the value of networking and treating everyone around me as equal human beings and listen and solve problems in a calm manner.
